title: identity.mfa.disabled payload
description: The `data` payload of the `identity.mfa.disabled` event: a user turned their second factor off with a valid factor of their own, and there is no other way to reach this from identity. Two fields against the three on `identity.mfa.enabled`, and the missing one is a fact rather than an oversight: the credential row is DELETED in the same transaction that appends this event, so a `credential_id` here would be a reference to a row a consumer can never look up. The row is gone; the event is the record that it was there. There is no `reason` either, and that omission is the publisher's judgement rather than a gap: "why" is operator-facing context typed by a human at a call site — a lost phone, a support ticket — and a field whose values vary per operator is a field every consumer learns to ignore. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

user_id.description: The user the factor belonged to. Always equal to the envelope's `subject`. A bare uuid rather than a `usr_`-prefixed id: that is what identity's `id.UUID.String()` produces, and it is the same value courier and billing already key users on (D7).

method.description: Which kind of factor went off. The same closed set of one as on `identity.mfa.enabled`, and for the same reason: the `mfa_credentials` table carries `CHECK (method = 'totp')`. Worth having on the revocation when the id is not — a consumer can at least tell that a time-based code stopped working, which is the fact a support conversation turns on.
